structure.note: One class of shares, but registered shares held for more than three years carry double voting rights (247,156,822 of the 496,391,012 shares with voting rights at December 31, 2025). The Arnault family group, controlled through Agache SCA (whose managing general partner is Bernard Arnault), held 49.77% of the share capital and 65.89% of the voting rights exercisable at Shareholders' Meetings: 42.17% / 56.26% via Christian Dior SE and 7.60% / 9.63% directly and via other family companies. The URD states that, to the Company's knowledge, no other shareholder held 5% or more.

notes: All figures from the LVMH 2025 Universal Registration Document (fiscal year ended December 31, 2025), the PDF hosted on LVMH's own content CDN (lvmh-com.cdn.prismic.io, linked from lvmh.com/en/investors). EUR, converted exactly from EUR millions. OWNERSHIP: Bernard Arnault personally holds 946,055 shares ('in a personal capacity', Board membership as of December 31, 2025); the URD gives no percentage, so pctEconomic is null (for reference only, about 0.19% of the 497,686,940 shares; not disclosed). The relevant holding is the Arnault family group's 49.77% of share capital (65.89% of votes exercisable at Shareholders' Meetings; 65.77% of theoretical votes), recorded in family. That figure includes Christian Dior SE's 42.17%, so Christian Dior SE is not listed separately. Whether Bernard Arnault's personal shares are inside the family-group total is not stated; they are not added. Relation is 'chair' (Chairman and CEO since 1989; reappointed by the Board on April 17, 2025). CDC: the URD gives the CDC Group's 1.24% (and CDC's direct 1%) as of its last threshold crossing on April 16, 2025, not December 31; the group figure is used and the direct 1% is not added to it. Percentages of share capital include the 1,295,928 treasury shares (0.26%) in the denominator. About 900,000 shareholders in total (Euroclear survey, December 2025). BUYBACKS: EUR 1,320.8m paid for 2,550,539 shares bought to be retired (parent-company note 13.1), the same rule as last year: purchases covering bonus share plans (579,981 shares, EUR 320.4m) and the liquidity contract (394,947 shares, round-trip) are not counted as cash returned to shareholders. This ties to §4.1.1 (517,973 shares at an average EUR 585.62 plus 2,032,566 at EUR 500.58, all for 'shares pending retirement'). It includes the EUR 1 billion programme of February–November 2025 (1,899,397 shares; note 16.3) plus 651,142 further shares bought for retirement. For reference: gross purchases of all kinds were 3,525,467 shares, EUR 1,863m (cash impact EUR 1,862m, note 16.3), and the cash-flow statement shows a net 'Acquisition and disposal of LVMH shares' of EUR (1,640)m inside 'Other equity-related transactions'. 2,654,760 shares were retired in 2025. DIVIDENDS: EUR 6,465m paid by LVMH SE; the cash-flow line of EUR (7,123)m also includes EUR 414m paid to minority interests and EUR 244m of tax on intra-group dividends, both excluded. STOCK COMP: Note 17.4 expense of EUR 165m, all bonus share plans (no LVMH Shares expense in 2025). PLAN: the URD describes the 2024 LVMH Shares offer and says employees held the equivalent of less than 1% of the share capital at December 31, 2025, in employee savings plans and as registered bonus shares.

taxes.notes: Taxes: the consolidated cash flow statement's own 'TOTAL TAX PAID' (EUR 4,901m), which covers tax paid in operating activities (EUR 4,656m), tax paid related to interim and final dividends (EUR 244m, on intra-group dividends, in financing activities) and tax on investment disposals (nil); the printed parts sum to 4,900, so the total carries rounding. Operating-only figure would be 4.66. R&D: LVMH reports no R&D line in the income statement; the management report gives research and development investments of EUR 200m (mainly scientific research for skincare and makeup in Perfumes and Cosmetics); the accounting policy states research expenditure is not capitalized, so it is treated as expensed.

paidout.notes: FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025), IFRS, from the 2025 Universal Registration Document. Interest paid on debt and on leases (290 + 545) and operating tax paid (4,656) sit inside operating activities; only the 244 of dividend-related tax in financing is added. The statement's 'TOTAL TAX PAID' is 4,901; the two printed parts sum to 4,900 (rounding, and nil tax on investment disposals). Capex uses gross PP&E and intangible purchases from note 15.3 rather than the net 'Operating investments' line. revenueIncludesExcise is null: the revenue policy says revenue is net of all forms of discount but does not say whether excise duties on Wines and Spirits are included or deducted. Lease principal (2,974) noted, not added. FX: calendar-2025 average.

marketcap.notes: One class of shares, priced from its primary listing on Euronext Paris (MC.PA) in EUR rather than the U.S. OTC ADR. Shares = 494,606,080 total shares − 743,358,184 gross + 739,382,278 net voting rights (parts signed so they sum to shares) = 494,606,080 − 3,975,906 = 490,630,174 at October 31, 2026. The monthly disclosure states no treasury count. Gross minus net voting rights equals the shares deprived of voting rights, which are the treasury shares: the same identity gives exactly the 1,295,928 treasury shares the 2025 URD reports at December 31, 2025 (744,843,762 theoretical − 743,547,834 exercisable votes). If a stated figure is preferred, the total including treasury shares is 494,606,080 (treasury about 0.8%). Share count fell from 497,686,940 at December 31, 2025 as LVMH retired repurchased shares.
